The forward problem is described by the time-harmonic Maxwell equations with the refractive index as the unknown.
The inverse problem is to reconstruct the refractive index given far field measurements for many incident waves.
The inverse problem is highly ill-conditioned, so regularization methods must be used to handle data noise.
The paper considers the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm and the iteratively regularized Gauss-Newton method (IRGNM).
Spectral preconditioning is used to accelerate the iterative solution of the regularized Newton equations.
The spectral preconditioner is constructed using the connection between the conjugate gradient method and Lanczos' method.
Updating the preconditioner during the Newton iteration is important to maintain efficiency as the regularization parameter decreases.
The Lepski-type stopping rule is used to choose the optimal stopping index, balancing the residual and propagated data noise error.
For exact data, the updated preconditioned IRGNM outperforms Landweber iteration and Newton-CG.
For noisy data, the Lepski-type stopping rule performs considerably better than the discrepancy principle.
The paper uses 25 incident waves and 100 far field measurements, resulting in a data vector of size 5000.
The unknown refractive index is represented using 500 to 2000 coefficients.
The forward problem is solved using a fast solver for the electromagnetic Lippmann-Schwinger equation.
The numerical examples use a wave number of κ = 1 and consider a refractive index perturbation within a unit cube.
The relative noise level in the random noise experiments is about 2%.
